fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Is a Dental Abscess?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A dental abscess is a collection of pus caused by a bacterial infection. There are two main types:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A periapical abscess forms at the tip of a tooth's root, usually when decay, a crack or injury allows bacteria to reach the nerve.

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A periodontal abscess forms in the gum and bone beside a tooth, often associated with gum disease.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Infection can also develop around a partially erupted wisdom tooth. An abscess will not resolve on its own. Even if the pain eases, the infection may still be present and spreading.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Important

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: When to Seek Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Contact us urgently if you notice:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Severe, persistent or throbbing toothache

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Swelling in your gum, face or jaw

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A pimple-like bump on your gum that may release fluid

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A bad taste or unpleasant smell in your mouth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Pain when biting or tenderness to touch

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Fever or feeling generally unwell

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Call 000 or go to your nearest hospital emergency department immediately if you have swelling that affects your breathing or swallowing, swelling spreading to your eye or neck, a high fever, or difficulty opening your mouth.

sections.label: What to Do Before Your Appointment

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What to Do Before Your Appointment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Rinse gently with warm salt water several times a day, and take over-the-counter pain relief as directed if suitable for you. Use a cold compress on the outside of your face. Avoid applying heat to the swelling, do not squeeze or pierce the area, and avoid very hot or cold food and drink.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We examine the area, check your temperature and general health, and take digital X-rays to identify the source of the infection. Our first priority is relieving your pain and controlling the infection. Depending on the cause, this may involve draining the abscess, beginning root canal therapy to clean the infected tooth, cleaning beneath the gum as part of gum and periodontal treatment, or tooth extraction if the tooth cannot be saved. Antibiotics may be prescribed in some situations, such as when infection has spread or you are unwell, but they are not a substitute for treating the source.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Take any prescribed medication exactly as directed, and continue warm salt water rinses. Contact us if swelling increases or you develop a fever. It is important to attend all follow-up appointments to complete treatment, as the infection can return if the cause is not fully addressed.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for a Dental Abscess

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for a Dental Abscess

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We prioritise urgent appointments for patients with signs of infection and use digital X-rays to diagnose the source quickly. Our team explains each option clearly and works gently, with happy gas available for patients who feel anxious.

sections.label: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Small label
fields.value: FAQ

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can a dental abscess go away on its own?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No. Even if the abscess drains or the pain settles, the infection usually remains and can return or spread without treatment.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Will antibiotics cure an abscess?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Antibiotics may help control spreading infection, but they do not remove the source. Dental treatment is needed to resolve the problem.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Is a dental abscess dangerous?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: It can be. In rare cases, infection can spread to other areas of the head and neck. Seek hospital care if swelling affects breathing or swallowing.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Will I lose my tooth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Not necessarily. Many abscessed teeth can be saved with root canal therapy. We will discuss the options after examining the tooth.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Why has the pain suddenly stopped?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Pain may stop if the nerve has died or the abscess has drained, but the infection is still likely to be present.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can I have treatment if my face is swollen?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes. We can assess and begin managing the infection. In some cases, swelling needs to settle before certain treatments.
